title: Embedding evaluation & graceful-fallback workshop playbook
summary: Working playbook for a 3-hour customer-facing workshop focused on evaluating embedding quality, latency/cost tradeoffs, and designing fallback strategies for production POCs. Includes agenda, slide skeleton, facilitator prompts, risk checklist, and next-step acceptance criteria.
agenda: 0:00-0:10 — Welcome, objectives, success criteria (host + customer expectations)
0:10-0:25 — Current architecture & dataset overview (customer presents quick snapshot)
0:25-0:60 — Embedding quality primer: metrics and failure modes (short lecture + Q&A)
0:60-1:25 — Hands-on eval: sample queries vs candidate embedding configs (paired exercise)
1:40-2:05 — Latency/cost tradeoff lab: quantization, batch sizing, and retrieval caching
2:05-2:35 — Fallback design session: policy sketch (region/model/approximate retrieval fallbacks)
2:35-2:50 — Runbook & monitoring quick-draft (what to alert on, SLOs, signal dashboards)
2:50-3:00 — Close: decisions, owners, immediate next steps, and success criteria for POC go/no-go

Slide 10: POC acceptance criteria and next steps
facilitator_notes: Before the session: request 3 representative user queries + 200 sample docs from the customer (anonymized). Precompute a baseline embedding snapshot so the hands-on flows start fast.
Kickoff: be explicit about what we can and cannot prove in a single session. Align on what 'success' looks like (e.g., >0.7 P@10 on key user queries, p95 retrieval < 120ms).
During hands-on: split attendees into two teams — one focuses on quality (different embedder configs), other on infra (latency/cost).
Keep a running living doc of observed failure cases (copy rows: query, expected doc, retrieved doc, notes). This becomes the initial eval prompt set.
If vector DB access is slow, switch to local approximate ANN (FAISS) fallback demo — show how recall changes but latency improves.
For the fallback session: use a simple decision tree template (region/availability model) rather than trying to engineer a full state machine in-session.
Timebox every activity. If exercises slip, skip deeper parameter sweeps and capture configs to test post-workshop.
End with concrete owners and a 2-week checklist: ingest pipeline, index refresh policy, monitoring dashboard, and a smoke-test harness for canary releases.
runbook_checklist: POC owner assigned (customer + Redwood SE contact)
Baseline evaluation dataset and golden queries stored in repo/drive
Vector DB config exported (index type, ef/search params, distance metric)
Embedding model versions pinned and artifacts stored (with quantization metadata)
Cache policy documented (prefix caching, TTLs, cache warm strategy)
Fallback policies defined and sanity-tested (ANN -> smaller model -> cached answer)
SLOs defined for retrieval latency, overall end-to-end p95, and quality metrics to track
Alerting knobs configured (e.g., recall drop > X% over 1h, retrieval latency > 2x baseline)
Smoke test harness: automated queries with expected top-3 IDs and tolerance thresholds
Security review checklist (PII in docs, key management for embeddings if customer requires)
Stakeholder cadence defined (weekly sync + a 30-day review)
risk_mitigation: Data availability: if sample data is delayed, use synthetic but realistic corpora and mark results as provisional
Latency surprises: prepare a cached-demo fallback for the demo path so UX does not break during session
Metric disagreements: predefine how to prioritize metrics (quality first for knowledge-heavy apps; latency for realtime chat)
Index drift: advise conservative refresh schedules for POC and instrument vector freshness metric
Security concerns: always offer a private-run option or redaction script if customer refuses to upload raw docs
prep_actions: Ask customer for dataset + sample queries 5 business days prior
Precompute baseline embeddings (3 model variants) and a performance snapshot
Provision a small vector DB instance with chosen index types and preload samples
Prepare a short demo notebook (Colab or internal notebook) that reproduces top-3 flows
Create workshop slide deck from skeleton and share with customer 48 hours before
Confirm attendees and roles (POC owner, data owner, infra owner, two engineers for hands-on)
breakout_tasks: Quality team: run P@5 and MRR on 20 golden queries across three embedding configs
Infra team: measure p50/p95 retrieval with different index params and batch sizes
Policy team: sketch a simple fallback decision tree and list required signals for routing
SEs: capture 5 reproducible failure examples to add to regression test set
Product: draft provisional acceptance criteria and rollout gating conditions
acceptance_criteria: Quality: For the customer golden set, top-5 precision improves over baseline or is acceptable per agreed threshold
Latency: End-to-end median retrieval for common queries < target (customer-specific; default 80ms), p95 < 300ms
Cost: Estimate for steady-state < agreed budget band or a documented plan to optimize
Observability: Dashboard with recall/latency/cost visible and alerts wired
Fallbacks: At least one tested fallback path with documented behavior and owner
